materials.title: My first choir concert
materials.text:
Our school choir ____1____ (meet) every Tuesday after lunch. I joined in September because I enjoyed singing at home. At the first meeting, I knew nobody except a girl from my maths class, so I sat beside her.

The teacher gave each of us two ____2____ (song) to practise. One was slow and the other was cheerful. I put the pages in a folder so they would not disappear ____3____ my school bag among loose homework sheets.

Before our first concert, we practised standing in two rows. I was shorter than most of the others, so the teacher asked ____4____ (I) to stand at the front. That made me nervous because there would be nobody in front of me to follow.

My friend told me ____5____ (look) at the conductor, not at her. The conductor's hands would help everyone begin together. I watched ____6____ (careful) as the teacher showed us how a small movement could signal a quiet ending.

On the concert day, I wore ____7____ white shirt and dark trousers. My parents arrived early, but I could not see them clearly from the stage. The lights above us were ____8____ (bright) than the lights over the seats.

When the music began, I forgot to search for familiar faces. I listened to the voices beside me and sang with them. After ____9____ (finish), we waited for the conductor to lower her hands. Only then did we turn ____10____ the audience and smile. My parents said they had heard me. I liked knowing that my voice had also belonged to a much larger sound.

questions.explanation: Collective choir may take singular meets or British notional plural meet. Meeting alone lacks an auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of song.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Pages can disappear in/inside the bag among other sheets. Of/from do not express this location.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of careful.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: White begins with consonant sound, so a. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of bright.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of finish.
questions.explanation: After finishing/having finished both fit completion before waiting. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.explanation: Turn to/towards/toward the audience directs attention and body to them. Of/from do not express that turn.

materials.title: A birthday card for the rabbit
materials.text:
My little brother ____1____ (love) our pet rabbit, Snow. He says Snow should have a birthday like everyone else in the family. We do not know the rabbit's real birthday, so we use the day she came to live with us.

This year, my brother made three little ____2____ (card). One was from him, one from me and one from our parents. I helped him write the names, but he drew all the pictures ____3____ himself. Each picture showed Snow eating or sleeping.

Mum reminded ____4____ (we) that a rabbit could not read a card. My brother said the pictures were for Snow and the words were for us. He put the cards on a shelf outside her enclosure, where she could not chew them.

We decided ____5____ (spend) some time making her play area interesting. Mum checked the materials and helped us arrange a cardboard tunnel. Snow moved through it ____6____ (slow), stopping at the far end to look around.

My brother wanted to give her ____7____ enormous piece of birthday cake. Mum explained that human cake was not suitable rabbit food. We kept her ordinary feeding routine and enjoyed the cake ourselves instead.

The tunnel was ____8____ (long) than the old one. Before ____9____ (leave) Snow to explore, we made sure she could move through and out comfortably. My brother sat quietly nearby rather than lifting her into it. He was pleased when she chose to enter again.

At the end of the day, the cards were still ____10____ the shelf. Snow had not read a word, but my brother had spent a happy afternoon thinking about what she actually liked. That seemed a good way to mark her special day.

questions.explanation: Singular brother in present habit takes loves. Base disagrees and loving lacks auxiliary.

materials.title: The lesson near the wall
materials.text:
I ____1____ (try) ice skating only once before my friend invited me to a lesson. My memory of that first visit was mostly of holding the wall. This time, I wanted to learn how to move without pulling myself along it.

The instructor asked everyone ____2____ (check) their skates before going onto the ice. A member of staff helped with the fit. We were divided into two groups so that people ____3____ had never skated could begin separately from those with some experience.

My group practised bending our knees and taking small steps. Falling was less frightening after we learned a suitable way to get up. The instructor gave the directions ____4____ (clear), then watched each person try instead of demonstrating once and disappearing.

There were several ____5____ (child) in the lesson as well as adults. Nobody was expected to move at exactly the same speed. I was more relaxed ____6____ I had been during my first visit, when I thought everyone else knew what to do.

After ____7____ (practise) near the side, I moved a short distance towards the middle with the instructor's guidance. My arms ____8____ (hold) out for balance. I was not graceful, but I was no longer using the wall as a handle.

My friend waited ____9____ me beside the exit after her own lesson. We agreed to return the following week. It was an ____10____ (importance) beginning, not evidence that I could already do every movement safely. For the moment, a few independent steps were enough to make me want to learn more.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of try.
questions.explanation: Only one experience before later invitation takes had tried in the intended prior-past account. Base and unaided -ing do not fit; unlisted tense readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: Asked everyone takes to check. Other forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: People is subject antecedent, who/that. Which normally nonhuman and where not subject.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of clear.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of child.
questions.explanation: Several requires children. Singular/nonstandard plural do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: More relaxed than forms comparison. Then temporal and that not the comparative conjunction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of practise.
questions.explanation: After -ing or perfect -ing fits. British/American variants both accepted; base/past/to-infinitive do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of hold.
questions.explanation: Plural arms receive holding, were held. Held lacks auxiliary and was disagrees; other valid tense readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Waited for me takes for. Of/to do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of importance.
questions.explanation: Important is the adjective modifying beginning. Importance is a noun and importantly an adverb.

materials.title: The stamp with a strange animal
materials.text:
My uncle ____1____ (collect) stamps since he was at school. When I visited him last month, he showed me an album arranged by country. Some stamps were brightly coloured, while others used only two or three shades.

I noticed an animal ____2____ I could not name. It had a long nose and a heavy-looking body. My uncle did not ask me to guess forever. He showed me where the country's name was printed and suggested ____3____ (look) for reliable information about its wildlife.

We found several ____4____ (picture) of the animal, a tapir. The stamp was a simplified design rather than a photograph. It made the shape recognisable without showing every detail that a wildlife guide might include.

My uncle asked me to handle the album ____5____ (careful). Some pages had old paper that could tear. We looked at the stamp without peeling it from its place, and he used a pointer rather than pressing a finger onto its surface.

The album ____6____ (keep) in a closed cupboard when it was not in use. I had expected a collection to be mainly about buying things, but he spent a great deal of time reading ____7____ the places and events shown on them.

Before ____8____ (leave), I chose one modern spare stamp to start a small page of my own. It was ____9____ ordinary stamp, not a rare or valuable one. I wrote down where it came from and what its design showed. The first entry made ____10____ (I) curious about the next, although I knew a collection would need room and care as well as enthusiasm.

materials.title: The forecast before the match
materials.text:
Our school football match ____1____ (postpone) after heavy rain made the field unsuitable for play. I had seen a forecast showing only a small chance of rain and felt annoyed. I thought the forecast had promised us a dry afternoon.

The geography teacher asked me ____2____ (read) the wording again. A probability was not a promise that an event could never happen. Even a low chance did not rule ____3____ rain on some occasions. The meaning was less simple than the picture of a small sun had suggested.

We compared several weather ____4____ (report), noting their locations and publication times. A forecast made earlier could differ from a later update. We also checked whether the area described was the whole district or the particular place where our school stood.

After ____5____ (discuss) the examples, I understood why a screenshot without a time could be misleading. The teacher explained the distinction ____6____ (patient), without suggesting that every forecast was equally useful or that prediction was pointless.

The rescheduled match was arranged ____7____ the following Wednesday. This time, I checked the latest information and listened to the school's decision about the field. A dry sky at one moment did not automatically make the ground suitable.

We brought ____8____ (we) equipment only after the teacher confirmed the plan. It was ____9____ sensible arrangement because the people responsible could assess conditions we could not judge from a symbol on a screen. I still wanted accurate forecasts, but I now checked ____10____ (exact) what they said before turning them into a guarantee about my own afternoon.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of postpone.
questions.explanation: Singular match receives postponement. Postponed lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.explanation: Rule out rain means exclude its possibility. Rule in would mean include it, contrary to the not-excluded point.

materials.title: The bottle at the water’s edge
materials.text:
During a supervised beach clean, our class ____1____ (find) a glass bottle near the water. At first I wanted to pick it up quickly, but the teacher reminded us to follow the collection instructions. We had been told which objects required an adult's help.

The pupil ____2____ gloves were beside the bag called the teacher over. The bottle was intact, yet the teacher checked the surrounding sand before lifting it. A clean-looking object did not prove that there were no sharp ____3____ (piece) nearby.

We recorded the categories of rubbish rather than everyone's name beside each item. That made it possible ____4____ (compare) the kinds of material collected without turning the task into a competition about who had found the most.

Some objects ____5____ (leave) for trained staff because our group was not equipped to handle them. We marked their locations as instructed. Helping did not mean taking on every task ourselves, especially when the risks were different ____6____ those of ordinary litter.

After ____7____ (finish) our section, we checked the bags with the organisers. The results were explained ____8____ (clear), including the fact that one morning's collection could not show all the rubbish arriving along the coast over a year.

We washed ____9____ (we) hands and looked back at the beach. It was ____10____ encouraging change in one place, not a complete solution to marine litter. The next step was to understand what could prevent some of those objects from reaching the shore. Carrying a bag had made the problem visible; it had also given us questions that a single cleanup could not answer.
